long_biography.plain_text:
Polys Haji-Ioannou began managing oil tankers from Norway in 1993, continuing a business tradition established by his father, shipping entrepreneur Loucas Haji-Ioannou. Polyar Tankers manages tankers controlled by Polys, giving him a direct operating role in shipping rather than merely a passive interest in the family fortune.

His wealth now rests on more than shipping. He holds a substantial easyJet stake through his own holding vehicle, and the airline shares are the largest documented component of his fortune. That position makes him a shareholder, not the airline's founder or operator. He also has substantial real-estate investments. Polys's record is therefore distinct from both the easy-brand ventures created by Stelios Haji-Ioannou and Safe Bulkers, whose similarly named chief executive is the son of a different shipping family.

uncertainties.detail: Safe Bulkers' chairman and chief executive is a different Polys Hajioannou. The company's SEC filing identifies that executive as age 59 in 2026, names his father as Vassos and traces his career to Safety Management's predecessor. This dossier's Polys was born in 1959, is the son of Loucas and operates through Polyar Tankers. The Wikipedia article appears to conflate the two men, so its Safe Bulkers claims are rejected.

Formal company disclosures establish Polys's substantial shareholding through his own controlled vehicle. They do not identify him as easyJet's founder, executive or operator; those achievements are not transferred from Stelios Haji-Ioannou.

Polys received an economic platform created by the family's tanker fortune, supporting Inherited origin. He nevertheless has a directly evidenced operating career managing and controlling his own tanker interests through Polyar, which is retained in the biography and relationship summary.

Shipping created the original family fortune and remains an active operating business. Forbes currently identifies easyJet as the main source of Polys's wealth, so Aviation & Aerospace is used for primary industry while Shipping & Maritime is retained for wealth creation.

Companies House supports September 1959, consistent with Forbes's current age and the input's age in 2020. No reliable source located supplies the exact day, and no place more specific than the existing Cyprus birth country is proposed.

No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website was verified. The official Polyar site and dedicated Forbes profile are proposed. The existing Wikipedia link is retained as input context but its conflated Safe Bulkers section should not be used.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, private-family trivia and vessel-specific research are excluded. Family relationships appear only where necessary to explain inherited wealth and prevent achievement or namesake conflation.
